MR. YATIN OZA, SR. ADV. WITH ANURAG R RATHOR(9315) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 ORTIS LAW OFFICES(12342) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 NOTICE SERVED for the Respondent(s) No. 2,3,4 MS DIVYANGANA JHALA, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE HASMUKH D. SUTHAR  Date : 13/06/2024  ORAL ORDER 1.

sentences.text:
This application is filed for transferring of the investigation in relation to the FIR No.
11217030240258 of 2024 registered with Siddhpur Police Station, Patan, for the offence punishable under Sections 376(1), 328, etc. of the IPC.

2. Heard Mr. Yatin Oza, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. Anurag Rathor, learned advocate appearing for applicant and Ms. Divyangana Jhala, learned APP for the respondent State.
3. Learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that on 02.11.2021, the petitioner received a phone call from her friend, Khushbuben Mukeshkumar Babulal Gupta, who informed her about an event involving two local fortune NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/7228/2022 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined tellers ("Bhuvajis") in Village Vaghna near Siddhpur, where money Amitaben D/O Rajubhai Surtaji Purohit vs State Of Gujarat on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158693850/
1 was to be showered.
The petitioner and Khushbuben traveled from Palanpur to Chappi, where they met Ujefabhai and Shabirbhai.
They were told by Rakesh Sharma that two "Bhuvajis" had come to Vaghna for the ceremony.
Upon arrival at the farm, the petitioner and Khushbuben were informed they would participate in the ceremony.
Around 3 PM, one of the "Bhuvajis," Sureshbhai, took the petitioner into a room and locked the door.
He told her she needed to undergo a body purification process that night.
At around 9:30 PM, Sureshbhai gave her a liquid to drink, which made her dizzy and unconscious.
When she regained some consciousness around midnight, she found herself naked and in pain.
Sureshbhai threatened her not to disclose the incident.
On 05.12.2021, the petitioner attempted to file an FIR against the 'Bhuvajis' for rape at Palanpur City Police Station, but the police did not register her complaint.
Instead, a false complaint for extortion was lodged against her by the accused persons.
It is submitted that the police despite several attempts made by the petitioner to lodge an FIR against the accused persons for the offence of rape, the police authority did not pay the attention.
In this regard the petitioner made a representation dated 17.01.2022 to the respondent No.2 and representation dated 25.02.2022 to the respondent No.4, but they are yet to be considered.

Therefore, learned Senior Advocate requested to transfer the case to the CID (Crime).
4.
Learned APP appearing for the State has submitted that the investigation is still ongoing and the police are thoroughly and impartially investigating the case.

In view of the above, the NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/7228/2022 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined learned APP has requested to dismiss the petition, as the investigation is being properly conducted by the police and there is no need to transfer the case to the CID or any other investigating agency.

5. Having heard the learned advocates for the respective parties and having gone through the documents on record and considered the facts of the case, it appears that the investigation is still ongoing and the police are still recording statements and collecting evidence.

This court has also perused the order dated 08.05.2024 passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court, wherein the Court has directed to conduct an investigation under the supervision of Dy.S.P., Patan.
6.

So far as the transfer of the case to the CID is concerned, this Court deems it proper to refer to the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kusumben Patel Varun Punia v. The State of Uttarakhand and Ors, passed in SLP (Cri) No. 5930 of 2023, and in the case of Himansu Kumar v.
State of Chhattisgarh, reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 598, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that not every case of improper investigation can be transferred to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

sentences.text: Hence, no case is made out to transfer the matter to the CBI merely based on the defacto complainant's allegations that the police are not investigating the matter impartially and properly.

7. As the investigation is still ongoing, the respondent authority is directed to ensure that the investigation is conducted by an officer not below the rank of Deputy NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/7228/2022 ORDER DATED: 13/06/2024 undefined Superintendent of Police under the supervision of Superintendent of Police.

The Deputy Superintendent of Police is directed to consider the representation of the petitioner preferably within six weeks from the date of receipt of this order,
in accordance with the law, and conduct an impartial and fair investigation in the matter.
